outcome: birth trauma (subgaleal hemorrhage, soft tissue injury, cephalhematoma)
cohort: The study included 717 term neonates admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Saint Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
finding: The prevalence of birth trauma among term neonates admitted to the NICU was 12.3%, with subgaleal hemorrhage being the most common type (77.3%), and birth trauma was associated with significant morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Instrumental delivery was a factor associated with birth trauma, while elective caesarian section was protective against it.
